The region occupies most of the country's `dry zone' where annual railfall is lowest and variable and temperature generally found highest. Mean annual rainfall increases eastward and southward across the region, from <1400 mm in west, >1600 mm in east and >1800 mm in extreme south. geographical_description: This small distinctive region occupies the whole of St. Martin's island in the extreme north of the country. Very gently undulating old beach ridges and inter-ridges depressions, surrounded by sandy beaches. The soils are developed entirely in old and young coral beach sands. Mean annual rainfall may be about 3500 mm. Of total area (804 ha) 33% high, 63% medium high, 2% medium low land and remaining 2% homestead & water bodies.
name: 24. St. Martin’s Coral Island

main_agricultural_practices: Of net cropped area (75%) 75% irrigated and 9%, 49% & 31% are single, double & tripple cropped area . Major cropping patterns are: a) Boro-Fallow-T. Aman b) Mustard-Boro-T. Aman c) Potato-Boro-T. Aman d) Sugarcane+Potato e) Potato-Fallow-T. Aman f) Wheat/Maize-T. Aman-Fallow. The present cropping intensity is 215%. Other popularly grown crops are Cabbage, Cauliflower, Tomato, Gourds, Cucurbits etc.
administratrative_units: Dinajpur, Gaibandha, Joypurhat, Bogra, Naogaon, Sirajganj and Natore
geographical_description: This region is developed over Madhupur clay. It occupies about 80% of the barind tract. The area is in north western parts of the country. Relief is locally irregular near entrenched river channels, with shallow gulleys; ellevation gradually increase towards west and merge with high barind tract. The predominant soils have a grey, silty, puddled topsoil and ploughpan. The mean annual ranfall is highest in the north-east (2000 mm) and lowest in south-west (1300-1500 mm). Of total area (504854 ha) 30% high, 55% medium high, 4% medium low, 2% low land and remaining 9% homestead & water bodies.
name: 25. Level Barind Tract

main_agricultural_practices: Of net cropped area (77%) 71% irrigated and 18%, 49% & 32% are single, double & tripple cropped area . Aman. The present cropping intensity is 215%. Other popularly grown crops are Tomato, Mustard, Maize, Jute, Kaon, gourds etc.
administratrative_units: Rajshahi, Nawabganj, and Naogaon
geographical_description: It includes the western part of the barind tract where the underlying Madhupur clay has been uplifted and cut into by deep valleys. It occupies about 10% of the whole barind tract.It has short, deep valleys descending to the Ganges, Mahananda and Purnabhaba floodplains to the south and west. The region has predominantly poorly drained soils. The region lies in the dryest part of the country in north-west. Mean annual rainfall is about 1300 - 1400 mm. Of total area (1600 ha) 93% high, 1% medium high land and remaining 11% homestead & water bodies.
name: 26. High Barind Tract

main_agricultural_practices: Of net cropped area (75%) 78% irrigated and 5%, 52% & 39% are single, double & tripple cropped area . Other popularly grown crops are Sesame, Brinjal, Cabbage etc.
administratrative_units: Dinajpur, Rangpur, Gaibandha, Joypurhat, and Bogra
geographical_description: It occupies 10% of the barind tract in several discontinuous areas on its northern and eastern margins. Small interior areas lie slightly higher than adjoining level barind tract land and have been slightly dissected. In most areas, the relief is smooth and almost level. Mean annual rainfall is higher in the north-east (about 2000 mm) and decreases to around 1800 mm in western and southern areas. Of total area (107926 ha) 36% high, 56% medium high, 1% medium low land and remaining 7% homestead & water bodies.
name: 27. North Eastern Barind Tract

main_agricultural_practices: Of net cropped area (70%) 61% irrigated and 28%, 50% & 21% are single, double & tripple cropped area . Major cropping patterns are: a) Boro-T. Aus-T. Aman b) Boro-Fallow-T. Aman c) Mustard-B. Aus-Fallow d) Lentil/Chickpea-Jute-Fallow e) Fallow-B. Aus-T. Aman. The present cropping intensity is 193%. administratrative_units: Dhak, Gazipur, Narsingdi, Narayanganj, Tangail, Mymensingh and Kishoreganj
geographical_description: It lies in central part of the country. This is a region of complex relief and soils developed over the Modhupur clay. Level upland areas with deep, mainly well drained red and brown soils. There are valleys with deep & shallow, poorly drained, grey, silty soils.Rainfall is higher in the north than the south. Mean annual rainfall increases from around 2000 mm in the south to >2300 mm in the north. Of total area (424359 ha) 56% high, 18% medium high, 7% medium low, 9% low land and remaining 10% homestead & water bodies.
name: 28. Madhupur Tract

main_agricultural_practices: Of net cropped area (33%) 25% irrigated and 44%, 45% & 11% are single, double & tripple cropped area . Major cropping patterns are: a) Boro-Fallow-T. Aman b) Gourds/Cucumber-Fallow-T. Aman c) Country bean-Fallow-T. Aman d) Cowpea-B. Aus-T. Aman e) Fallow-Fallow-T. Aman. The present cropping intensity is 168%. administratrative_units: Khagrachhari, Chittagong Hill Tracts, Bandarban, Chittagong, Cox’s Bazar, Habiganj & Moulivibazar
geographical_description: This region includes the country's hill areas, occupy about 12% area that extended from north-east to south-eastern tip of the country. Releif is complex. Hills have been dissected to different degrees over different rocks. In general, slopes are very steep (>45%), but more rolling releif occurs locally and a few low hills have flat summits. The major hill soils are yellow-brown to strong brown, permeable, friable, loamy, very strongly acid and low in moisture holding capacity. The region is characterized by very heavy monsoon rainfall. Mean annual rainfall exceeds 5000 mm on hills of north, 2000-2500 mm in west and 3500-4000 mm in south. Of total area (1817172 ha) 92% high, 2% medium high, 1% medium low land and remaining 5% homestead & water bodies.
name: 29. Northern and Eastern Hills

main_agricultural_practices: Of net cropped area (73%) 49% irrigated and 38%, 50% & 12% are single, double & tripple cropped area . Major cropping patterns are: a) Boro-Fallow-T. Aman b) Boro-B. Aman c) Fallow-B. Aman d) Sugarcane+Turmeric e) Potato-T. Aus-T. Aman. The present cropping intensity is 174%. Other popularly grown crops are Mustard, Jute, wheat etc.
administratrative_units: Brahmanbaria district & miner areas in Habiganj district
geographical_description: This small region occupies two areas on the eastern border of Brahmanbaria district and extends marginally into the south-west corner of Habiganj district. Mainly broad, level, upland areasstanding 3-6 m above broad piedmont valleys. Uplands are closely dissected in some places.Valley soils are grey, mottled, silt loams and silt clay loams in intermittently and shallowly flooded upper parts of valleys, and dark grey heavy clays and peat in deeply flooded lower basins. Of total area (11324 ha) 55% high, 11% medium high, 10% medium low, 15% low, 3% very low land and remaining 6% homestead & water bodies.
name: 30. Akhaura Terrace
